A 20-kg ingot of the Nb-Ti-Cr-Si-X alloy in this study was prepared from commercially pure elements by vacuum induction melting.
Cut pieces of the as-cast alloys were vacuum-encapsulated inside quartz tubes partially filled with argon prior to heat treatments.
Homogenization was carried out at 1300 °C and aging treatments were carried over the range of 900–1100 °C for various times.

Figure 4 shows the presence of Laves phase at the grain boundaries in the samples which were subjected to hot deformation. Its presence at grain boundaries, on one hand, arrested the grain growth of the b-phase and led to a finer grain size (~15 µm) subsequent to deformation, whereas, on other hand, formation of a continuous layer could make the material brittle at room temperature.

The bright-field micrograph shows the presence of two kinds of defects in the Laves phase. One with very high density of twins whereas the other with relatively thicker twins.

mechanisms.name: Laves phase formation via metastable precursor phases

evidence.quote: it is proposed that the initiation of formation of Laves phase starts with the distortion of the {110} of bcc followed by the formation of the O-phase. Subsequently, Cr atoms diffuse out to form tetrahedra around atoms like Hf, Zr, Nb and Ti which leads to the formation of the C14 structure. This C14 being unstable converts to the C15 structure with copious presence of planar defects.

mechanisms.name: room-temperature embrittlement by continuous grain-boundary Laves layer

evidence.quote: formation of a continuous layer could make the material brittle at room temperature
